### Robustness to Prior Noise

```{python filename="simf_degradation_stats.py"}
#| output: false
import mindmap as mm

# per explicit instruction, only the permutation experiment is shown here
# (deletion/addition still computed and saved by processing_simf.qmd's
# Statistics section, just not plotted or discussed in this document).
operator = "permutation"

deg_metrics = mm.metric.MetricSuite.load("./results/simf/degradation")

# --- localization error --- reference=sLORETA (doesn't degrade),
# competitors=CSET/wCSET: tests when a corrupted connectome makes CSET/
# wCSET perform significantly worse than using no connectome at all,
# rather than a relative CSET-vs-wCSET comparison. Identical call to the
# one already cached by processing_simf.qmd's Statistics section.
# phase="qrp" always (no pp counterpart exists for this metric).
deg_comparisons = deg_metrics.stat.build_comparisons(["sloreta"], ["cset", "wcset"])
pct_order = sorted(deg_metrics.to_df(metrics="localization_error", filters={"phase": "qrp"})["percentage"].unique())
loc_result = deg_metrics.stat.cluster_permutation(
    "localization_error", coord="percentage", group_by="Method", comparisons=deg_comparisons,
    pairing_col="region", coord_order=pct_order, higher_is_better=False, filters={"phase": "qrp"},
    n_permutations=3000, seed=0,
)
loc_clusters_cset = loc_result.clusters_by_pair[("sloreta", "cset")]
loc_clusters_wcset = loc_result.clusters_by_pair[("sloreta", "wcset")]

# --- spatial correlation --- same sLORETA-reference comparison as
# above. phase="qrp" always (no pp counterpart is computed for
# degradation, see degradation_reconstruction.py).
pct_order_c = sorted(deg_metrics.to_df(metrics="correlation", filters={"phase": "qrp"})["percentage"].unique())
corr_result = deg_metrics.stat.cluster_permutation(
    "correlation", coord="percentage", group_by="Method", comparisons=deg_comparisons,
    pairing_col="region", coord_order=pct_order_c, higher_is_better=True, filters={"phase": "qrp"},
    n_permutations=3000, seed=0,
)
corr_clusters_cset = corr_result.clusters_by_pair[("sloreta", "cset")]
corr_clusters_wcset = corr_result.clusters_by_pair[("sloreta", "wcset")]

# --- statistics quoted in the prose below --- selected by sign rather
# than by cluster position/count: how many clusters exist (and where)
# depends on the current simulation parameters (see
# parameter_estimates_review.md) and isn't safe to hard-code - a prior
# version of this cell assumed fixed counts per pair and broke (IndexError)
# once results/simf/degradation was regenerated under retuned physical
# parameters. Per cluster_permutation_mne's sign convention, sign=-1 means
# the competitor (CSET/wCSET) significantly beats sLORETA, sign=+1 means
# sLORETA significantly beats the competitor; `cluster_where` returns None
# when no cluster of that sign exists (currently the case for loc/wcset's
# "worse" cluster - see prose, wCSET no longer becomes significantly worse
# than sLORETA on localization error at any tested degradation level).
# main_cluster()'s own significance caveat applies to each cluster
# individually here too - corr/wcset's "worse" cluster does NOT survive FDR
# correction (p_corrected `0.069` > 0.05), so the prose below must describe
# it as a trend, not a significant effect.

def cluster_where(cluster_df, sign):
    """The cluster (if any) where the competitor significantly beats
    sLORETA (sign=-1) or sLORETA significantly beats the competitor
    (sign=1) - None if no such cluster exists in the current result."""
    rows = cluster_df[cluster_df["sign"] == sign]
    return rows.iloc[0] if not rows.empty else None

deg_loc_cset_better = cluster_where(loc_clusters_cset, -1)
deg_loc_cset_better_end = fmt_num(deg_loc_cset_better["percentage_end"], 0)
deg_loc_cset_better_p, deg_loc_cset_better_dz = fmt_p(deg_loc_cset_better["p_corrected"]), fmt_stat(deg_loc_cset_better["effect_size"])

deg_loc_cset_c = cluster_where(loc_clusters_cset, 1)
deg_loc_cset_p, deg_loc_cset_dz = fmt_p(deg_loc_cset_c["p_corrected"]), fmt_stat(deg_loc_cset_c["effect_size"])
deg_loc_cset_start = fmt_num(deg_loc_cset_c["percentage_start"], 0)

deg_loc_wcset_early = cluster_where(loc_clusters_wcset, -1)
deg_loc_wcset_early_end = fmt_num(deg_loc_wcset_early["percentage_end"], 0)
deg_loc_wcset_early_p, deg_loc_wcset_early_dz = fmt_p(deg_loc_wcset_early["p_corrected"]), fmt_stat(deg_loc_wcset_early["effect_size"])
deg_loc_wcset_worse = cluster_where(loc_clusters_wcset, 1)  # None under current results - see prose

deg_corr_cset_early = cluster_where(corr_clusters_cset, -1)
deg_corr_cset_early_p, deg_corr_cset_early_dz = fmt_p(deg_corr_cset_early["p_corrected"]), fmt_stat(deg_corr_cset_early["effect_size"])
deg_corr_cset_early_end = fmt_num(deg_corr_cset_early["percentage_end"], 0)
deg_corr_cset_late = cluster_where(corr_clusters_cset, 1)
deg_corr_cset_late_p, deg_corr_cset_late_dz = fmt_p(deg_corr_cset_late["p_corrected"]), fmt_stat(deg_corr_cset_late["effect_size"])
deg_corr_cset_late_start = fmt_num(deg_corr_cset_late["percentage_start"], 0)

deg_corr_wcset_early = cluster_where(corr_clusters_wcset, -1)
deg_corr_wcset_early_p, deg_corr_wcset_early_dz = fmt_p(deg_corr_wcset_early["p_corrected"]), fmt_stat(deg_corr_wcset_early["effect_size"])
deg_corr_wcset_early_end = fmt_num(deg_corr_wcset_early["percentage_end"], 0)
deg_corr_wcset_late = cluster_where(corr_clusters_wcset, 1)
deg_corr_wcset_late_p = fmt_p(deg_corr_wcset_late["p_corrected"])  # does not survive correction - quoted as a trend only

# localization/correlation medians quoted in prose - read from
# processing_simf.qmd's precomputed metadata["derived"], not recomputed here.
_perm_d = deg_metrics.metadata["derived"]
deg_loc_perm_wcset_lo, deg_loc_perm_wcset_hi = _perm_d["loc_wcset_0_60"]
deg_loc_perm_wcset_70 = _perm_d["loc_wcset_70"]
deg_loc_perm_wcset_100 = _perm_d["loc_wcset_100"]

deg_loc_perm_wcset_lo_s = fmt_num(deg_loc_perm_wcset_lo)
deg_loc_perm_wcset_hi_s = fmt_num(deg_loc_perm_wcset_hi)
deg_loc_perm_wcset_70_s = fmt_num(deg_loc_perm_wcset_70)
deg_loc_perm_wcset_100_s = fmt_num(deg_loc_perm_wcset_100)

deg_corr_perm_wcset_0 = fmt_num(_perm_d["corr_wcset_0"], 2)
deg_corr_perm_wcset_100 = fmt_num(_perm_d["corr_wcset_100"], 2)
_cset_lo, _cset_hi = _perm_d["corr_cset_0_60"]
deg_corr_perm_cset_lo = fmt_num(_cset_lo, 2)
deg_corr_perm_cset_hi = fmt_num(_cset_hi, 2)
deg_corr_perm_cset_100 = fmt_num(_perm_d["corr_cset_100"], 2)
```

In the simulation, the true connectome is known; in practice it never is exactly. To test what happens when the wrong connectome is used, we systematically permuted the true connectome before reconstruction (Section 2.3.3) and re-evaluated localization error and spatial correlation for CSET and wCSET, this time benchmarked directly against sLORETA rather than against each other: sLORETA is connectome-agnostic, so its performance cannot be affected by connectome corruption, making it a natural floor — the degradation level at which a connectivity-informed method becomes significantly worse than sLORETA is the point past which using the (corrupted) connectome is actively counterproductive, rather than merely less helpful. dSPM remains connectome-agnostic too and is shown only as a flat, untested reference line.

wCSET's localization error remained essentially flat under permutation up to 60% (`{python} deg_loc_perm_wcset_lo_s`–`{python} deg_loc_perm_wcset_hi_s` mm), only climbing noticeably beyond that point (`{python} deg_loc_perm_wcset_70_s` mm at 70%, `{python} deg_loc_perm_wcset_100_s` mm at 100%). Benchmarked against sLORETA (region-paired cluster-permutation), wCSET was significantly *more* accurate across low-to-moderate degradation (0–`{python} deg_loc_wcset_early_end`%, p_corrected `{python} deg_loc_wcset_early_p`, Cohen's dz = `{python} deg_loc_wcset_early_dz`), and never became significantly worse than sLORETA at any degradation level tested, including full (100%) permutation. CSET showed the same early advantage over a comparable range (0–`{python} deg_loc_cset_better_end`%, p_corrected `{python} deg_loc_cset_better_p`, dz = `{python} deg_loc_cset_better_dz`), but unlike wCSET this advantage reversed: CSET became significantly worse than sLORETA from `{python} deg_loc_cset_start`% onward (p_corrected `{python} deg_loc_cset_p`, dz = `{python} deg_loc_cset_dz`) — a degradation level at which wCSET's own localization error never reached a significant deficit, even under full connectome permutation.

```{python filename="simf_localization_degradation_plot.py"}

Markers are filled/solid where significantly different from sLORETA, tested at each degradation level (region-paired cluster-permutation). Dashed line: dSPM's undegraded-connectome reference level."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# flat reference: dSPM is connectome-agnostic (not recomputed per

# prose above).
deg_ref_loc = deg_metrics.metadata["derived"]["ref_loc"]

# two-pair result (sLORETA vs CSET, sLORETA vs wCSET) -> plot.cluster_permutation()
# dispatches to the compact multi-competitor overlay (same pattern as the
# noise-sweep figures above, simf_noise_stats.py), reference (sLORETA)
# auto-inferred from the group shared by both pairs.
deg_loc_fig, deg_loc_ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
deg_loc_fig, deg_loc_ax = deg_metrics.plot.cluster_permutation(
    loc_result, colors=COLORS, marker="o", markersize=4, ax=deg_loc_ax,
)
mark_reference(deg_loc_ax, "sloreta")
# dSPM stays a flat, untested reference line (still connectome-agnostic,
# just not part of this comparison) - sLORETA no longer needs one, it's
# plotted as its own tested curve above.
deg_loc_ax.axhline(deg_ref_loc["dspm"], color=COLORS["dspm"], linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, zorder=0.5)
deg_loc_ax.set_xlabel("Connectome degradation (%)")
deg_loc_ax.set_ylabel("Localization error (mm)")
deg_loc_ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

legend_handles = [
    Line2D([0], [0], color=COLORS["dspm"], linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, label="dspm (undegraded)"),
]
deg_loc_fig.legend(handles=legend_handles, loc="lower center", ncol=1, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.04))

deg_loc_fig.tight_layout()
```


Spatial correlation with the ground truth showed a similar but more pronounced pattern: permutation slowly degraded wCSET's correlation (`{python} deg_corr_perm_wcset_0` at 0% down to `{python} deg_corr_perm_wcset_100` at 100%), while CSET's own correlation stayed comparatively flat through 60% (`{python} deg_corr_perm_cset_lo`–`{python} deg_corr_perm_cset_hi`) before also declining sharply thereafter (`{python} deg_corr_perm_cset_100` at 100%). Against sLORETA, both methods started out significantly better (region-paired cluster-permutation: CSET 0–`{python} deg_corr_cset_early_end`%, p_corrected `{python} deg_corr_cset_early_p`, dz = `{python} deg_corr_cset_early_dz`; wCSET 0–`{python} deg_corr_wcset_early_end`%, p_corrected `{python} deg_corr_wcset_early_p`, dz = `{python} deg_corr_wcset_early_dz`), but only CSET's advantage reversed into a significant deficit, from `{python} deg_corr_cset_late_start`% onward (p_corrected `{python} deg_corr_cset_late_p`, dz = `{python} deg_corr_cset_late_dz`). wCSET's correlation, by contrast, never became significantly worse than sLORETA's, even at full permutation — its apparent dip at 100% did not reach significance (p_corrected `{python} deg_corr_wcset_late_p`).

### Surrogate alternatives

```{python filename="simf_surrogate_stats.py"}
#| output: false
import mindmap as mm

# beltrami replaced atlas-a2a/atlas-a2a-bin as of surrogate_reconstruction.py's
# latest run (see processing_simf.qmd) - kept in sync with the actual
# on-disk surrogate set, not the earlier atlas-a2a/-bin pair.
surrogates = ["beltrami", "fused", "fused-bin", "geom-atlas", "geom-atlas-bin"]
conditions = ["original"] + surrogates

# Reader-facing surrogate names differ from the on-disk `Surrogate` tags
# above - "fused" undersold the atlas provenance, and "geom-atlas" wrongly
# implied a population atlas (it's built purely from the subject's own
# mesh geometry) while also colliding with "geometry-only" language used
# elsewhere for the unrelated Beltrami-operator approach (Section 2.3.3).
# Data lookups/palette keys elsewhere still key off the original tags;
# only prose/inline-stat/axis text goes through this map.
SURROGATE_LABELS = {
    "fused": "atlas", "fused-bin": "atlas-bin",
    "geom-atlas": "local", "geom-atlas-bin": "local-bin",
}
methods = ["cset", "wcset"]

# Question of interest: does substituting a surrogate connectome change THIS
# method's own accuracy relative to using the real (original) connectome? -
# not whether cset differs from wcset (that's answered above, in
# simf_localization_error.py). One combined suite (original + every
# surrogate, tagged by `Surrogate`) is now built and saved by
# processing_simf.qmd's Statistics section - loaded here directly, never
# constructed ad-hoc; each panel below just filters it by `Method`/`phase`.
surr_metrics = mm.metric.MetricSuite.load("./results/simf/surrogates")
surr_comparisons = surr_metrics.stat.build_comparisons(["original"], surrogates)

# identical calls to the ones already cached by processing_simf.qmd's
# Statistics section. phase="qrp" always (no pp counterpart exists for
# this metric).
surr_loc_results = {}
for method in methods:
    surr_loc_results[method] = surr_metrics.stat.wilcoxon(
        "localization_error", group_by="Surrogate",
        comparisons=surr_comparisons, pairing_col="region",
        filters={"Method": method, "phase": "qrp"},
    )

# statistics quoted in the prose below.
def _loc_row(method, surrogate):
    return competitor_row(surr_loc_results[method], surrogate, reference="original")

loc_wcset_p = {s: fmt_p(_loc_row("wcset", s)["p_corrected"]) for s in surrogates}
loc_wcset_r = {s: fmt_stat(_loc_row("wcset", s)["effect_size"]) for s in surrogates}

# Correlation: same "original vs. surrogate" pattern, filtering the same
# combined suite by (method, phase) per panel instead of loading a separate
# pre-built suite.
surr_ref_corr = surr_metrics.metadata["derived"]["ref_corr"]

# identical calls to the ones already cached by processing_simf.qmd's
# Statistics section.
surr_corr_results = {}
for phase in ["qrp", "pp"]:
    for method in methods:
        surr_corr_results[(method, phase)] = surr_metrics.stat.wilcoxon(
            "correlation", group_by="Surrogate",
            comparisons=surr_comparisons, pairing_col="region",
            filters={"Method": method, "phase": phase},
        )

# statistics quoted in the prose below.
def _corr_row(method, phase, surrogate):
    return competitor_row(surr_corr_results[(method, phase)], surrogate, reference="original")

corr_wcset_beltrami_qrp, corr_wcset_beltrami_pp = _corr_row("wcset", "qrp", "beltrami"), _corr_row("wcset", "pp", "beltrami")
corr_wcset_beltrami_r_lo = fmt_stat(min(abs(corr_wcset_beltrami_qrp["effect_size"]), abs(corr_wcset_beltrami_pp["effect_size"])))
corr_wcset_beltrami_r_hi = fmt_stat(max(abs(corr_wcset_beltrami_qrp["effect_size"]), abs(corr_wcset_beltrami_pp["effect_size"])))

corr_wcset_beltrami_qrp_median = fmt_num(surr_metrics.metadata["derived"]["wcset_beltrami_qrp_median"], 2)
corr_wcset_beltrami_pp_median = fmt_num(surr_metrics.metadata["derived"]["wcset_beltrami_pp_median"], 2)
corr_dspm_qrp_ref = fmt_num(surr_ref_corr["qrp"]["dspm"], 2)
corr_dspm_pp_ref = fmt_num(surr_ref_corr["pp"]["dspm"], 2)
corr_sloreta_qrp_ref = fmt_num(surr_ref_corr["qrp"]["sloreta"], 2)
corr_sloreta_pp_ref = fmt_num(surr_ref_corr["pp"]["sloreta"], 2)

corr_wcset_fused_qrp, corr_wcset_fused_pp = _corr_row("wcset", "qrp", "fused"), _corr_row("wcset", "pp", "fused")
corr_wcset_fused_p_qrp, corr_wcset_fused_p_pp = fmt_p(corr_wcset_fused_qrp["p_corrected"]), fmt_p(corr_wcset_fused_pp["p_corrected"])
corr_wcset_fusedbin_qrp, corr_wcset_fusedbin_pp = _corr_row("wcset", "qrp", "fused-bin"), _corr_row("wcset", "pp", "fused-bin")
corr_wcset_fusedbin_p_qrp, corr_wcset_fusedbin_p_pp = fmt_p(corr_wcset_fusedbin_qrp["p_corrected"]), fmt_p(corr_wcset_fusedbin_pp["p_corrected"])
corr_wcset_geom_qrp, corr_wcset_geombin_qrp = _corr_row("wcset", "qrp", "geom-atlas"), _corr_row("wcset", "qrp", "geom-atlas-bin")
corr_wcset_geom_p_qrp = fmt_p(max(corr_wcset_geom_qrp["p_corrected"], corr_wcset_geombin_qrp["p_corrected"]))
corr_wcset_geom_pp, corr_wcset_geombin_pp = _corr_row("wcset", "pp", "geom-atlas"), _corr_row("wcset", "pp", "geom-atlas-bin")
corr_wcset_geom_p_pp = fmt_p(corr_wcset_geom_pp["p_corrected"])
corr_wcset_geombin_p_pp = fmt_p(corr_wcset_geombin_pp["p_corrected"])
```

In clinical settings, subject-specific dMRI is often unavailable. We therefore tested whether cruder, dMRI-free connectome surrogates (Section 2.3.3) could replace the true connectome without materially harming CSET/wCSET's accuracy, comparing each surrogate directly against the original connectome for each method.

For localization error, wCSET was significantly *more* accurate using every surrogate tested than using the true connectome itself, though with small-to-moderate effect sizes (paired Wilcoxon vs. original connectome, region-paired: beltrami p `{python} loc_wcset_p["beltrami"]`, r = `{python} loc_wcset_r["beltrami"]`; atlas p `{python} loc_wcset_p["fused"]`, r = `{python} loc_wcset_r["fused"]`; atlas-bin p `{python} loc_wcset_p["fused-bin"]`, r = `{python} loc_wcset_r["fused-bin"]`; local p `{python} loc_wcset_p["geom-atlas"]`, r = `{python} loc_wcset_r["geom-atlas"]`; local-bin p `{python} loc_wcset_p["geom-atlas-bin"]`, r = `{python} loc_wcset_r["geom-atlas-bin"]`). If anything, then, substituting any of these cruder surrogates for the true connectome slightly improves wCSET's localization accuracy, with no surrogate standing out as meaningfully better than the others. CSET showed the opposite sensitivity: only the beltrami surrogate produced a significant difference, and in CSET's case it was a genuine deficit rather than an improvement; the full CSET breakdown is reported in the supplementary material (<!-- supp figure (CSET localization error, surrogate vs. original connectome, mirroring the wCSET panel below) -->).

```{python filename="simf_localization_surrogate_plot.py"}
#| echo: false

Dashed lines mark dSPM's and sLORETA's true-connectome medians as reference. Stars mark significance vs. the original (true) connectome (Wilcoxon signed-rank, region-paired, FDR-corrected). CSET's equivalent comparison is reported in the supplementary material."

from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# Distinct palette from the method COLORS above - this figure's color axis is
# condition (original vs. surrogate), not method, so it needs its own key.
# "original" gets a neutral gray (the reference condition, not a "peer"

# palette.md slots 1/2/3/4/5 - blue/orange/aqua/yellow/magenta), which clears
# every adjacent-pair CVD/contrast gate in both light and dark mode.
CONDITION_COLORS = {
    "original": LINE_COLOR,
    "beltrami": "#2a78d6",
    "fused": "#eb6834",
    "fused-bin": "#1baf7a",
    "geom-atlas": "#eda100",
    "geom-atlas-bin": "#e87ba4",
}

surr_ref_loc = surr_metrics.metadata["derived"]["ref_loc"]

# wCSET only in the main text - CSET's equivalent panel is qualitatively
# similar (see prose) and moved to the supplementary material.
surr_loc_fig, surr_loc_ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(len(conditions) * 1.5, 5))

surr_loc_fig, surr_loc_ax = surr_metrics.plot.group_comparison(
    surr_loc_results["wcset"], order=conditions, palette=CONDITION_COLORS, points=False,
    showfliers=False, width=0.6, ax=surr_loc_ax,
)
for ref_method in ["dspm", "sloreta"]:
    surr_loc_ax.axhline(surr_ref_loc[ref_method], color=COLORS[ref_method], linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, zorder=0.5)
surr_loc_ax.set_xticks(range(len(conditions)))
surr_loc_ax.set_xticklabels(ref_labels([SURROGATE_LABELS.get(c, c) for c in conditions], "original"), rotation=45, ha="right")
surr_loc_ax.set_xlabel("")
surr_loc_ax.set_ylabel("Localization error (mm)")
surr_loc_ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

surr_loc_legend_handles = [
    Line2D([0], [0], color=COLORS[m], linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, label=f"{m} (original connectome)")
    for m in ["dspm", "sloreta"]
]
surr_loc_fig.legend(handles=surr_loc_legend_handles, loc="lower center", ncol=2, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.04))

plt.tight_layout()
```

Spatial correlation showed the same pattern: every surrogate produced a statistically significant *increase* in wCSET's correlation with the ground truth relative to the original connectome, at both the quarter rising phase and the peak (region-paired Wilcoxon vs. original connectome; all p_corrected < 0.05). Effect sizes were generally small at the quarter rising phase but grew substantially by the peak, most markedly for beltrami (r = `{python} corr_wcset_beltrami_r_lo`–`{python} corr_wcset_beltrami_r_hi`, quarter rising phase to peak) — wCSET's correlation using beltrami (median `{python} corr_wcset_beltrami_qrp_median` quarter rising phase, `{python} corr_wcset_beltrami_pp_median` peak), like every other surrogate, was still roughly 3–4× higher than dSPM's (`{python} corr_dspm_qrp_ref`, `{python} corr_dspm_pp_ref`) or sLORETA's (`{python} corr_sloreta_qrp_ref`, `{python} corr_sloreta_pp_ref`) own correlation with the true connectome. The remaining surrogates showed the same significant improvement at both phases (atlas: p_corrected `{python} corr_wcset_fused_p_qrp` quarter rising phase, p_corrected `{python} corr_wcset_fused_p_pp` peak; atlas-bin: p_corrected `{python} corr_wcset_fusedbin_p_qrp` quarter rising phase, p_corrected `{python} corr_wcset_fusedbin_p_pp` peak; local: p_corrected `{python} corr_wcset_geom_p_qrp` quarter rising phase, p_corrected `{python} corr_wcset_geom_p_pp` peak; local-bin: p_corrected `{python} corr_wcset_geom_p_qrp` quarter rising phase, p_corrected `{python} corr_wcset_geombin_p_pp` peak). CSET showed the opposite pattern: correlation was generally significantly *lower* than with the original connectome, with small effect sizes, most consistently for the local surrogate; the full CSET breakdown is reported in the supplementary material (<!-- supp figure (CSET spatial correlation, surrogate vs. original connectome, mirroring the wCSET panel below) -->).

Dashed lines mark dSPM's and sLORETA's true-connectome medians as reference. Stars mark significance vs. the original (true) connectome (Wilcoxon signed-rank, region-paired, FDR-corrected). CSET's equivalent comparison is reported in the supplementary material."
```{python filename="simf_correlation_surrogate_plot.py"}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

ref_methods = ["dspm", "sloreta"]
phase_titles = {"qrp": "Quarter rising phase", "pp": "Peak phase"}

# wCSET only in the main text - CSET's equivalent panels are qualitatively
# similar (see prose) and moved to the supplementary material.

for row_i, phase in enumerate(["qrp", "pp"]):

        showfliers=False, width=0.6, ax=ax,
    )
    for ref_method in ref_methods:
        ax.axhline(surr_ref_corr[phase][ref_method], color=COLORS[ref_method], linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, zorder=0.5)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(conditions)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(ref_labels([SURROGATE_LABELS.get(c, c) for c in conditions], "original"), rotation=45, ha="right")
    ax.set_xlabel("")
    ax.set_ylabel(f"{phase_titles[phase]}\nSpatial correlation")
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

surr_corr_legend_handles = [
    Line2D([0], [0], color=COLORS[m], linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, label=f"{m} (original connectome)")
    for m in ref_methods
]
surr_corr_fig.legend(handles=surr_corr_legend_handles, loc="lower center", ncol=2, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.04))

plt.tight_layout()
```


## Study II: Clinical Localization (Resection Cohort)

### Localization Error

```{python filename="results_resection_localization.py"}
#| output: false
import mindmap as mm

# METHODS/COLORS reused from plot_configuration.py above (same values) -
# MCE excluded from every study, see that cell's note. beltrami is added
# locally as a 6th method (RESECTION_METHODS) since it's only computed for
# the clinical cohorts, not Study I's simulation - see plot_configuration.py's
# note on METHOD_LABELS.
RESECTION_METHODS = METHODS + ["beltrami"]

# one MetricSuite for the whole cohort, built and stats-cached by
# processing_spike.qmd (resection_evaluation_metrics.py/spike_statistics.py)
# - loaded here directly, never built from a raw CSV.
resection_metrics = mm.metric.MetricSuite.load("./results/spike/resection")

# Excluded regardless of ILAE outcome - see processing_spike.qmd's Cohort
# Summary for the full breakdown (pat01: no usable resection mask AND no EEG
# channel locations; pat18: no real resection zone at all). Reproduced here
# (rather than read off the suite) so this cell's stat.wilcoxon() call below
# is byte-identical to the one processing_spike.qmd's spike_statistics.py
# already cached - without this, the call differs in its filters and silently
# recomputes over the wrong subject population instead of hitting the cache.
EXCLUDED_SUBJECTS = ["pat01", "pat18"]
all_subjects = resection_metrics.to_df(metrics="peak_distance_mm")["Subject"].unique()
included_subjects = [s for s in all_subjects if s not in EXCLUDED_SUBJECTS]

# seizure-free (ILAE=1) subjects, minus the exclusions above, quarter rising
# phase (the primary evaluation point) - per explicit instruction, no longer
# faceted across every surgical outcome level. The suite-native replacement
# for a manual df[(df["ILAE"]==1) & ~df["Subject"].isin(EXCLUDED_SUBJECTS)]
# filter.
FILTERS = {"phase": "qrp", "ILAE": 1, "Subject": included_subjects}
resection_n = resection_metrics.metadata["derived"]["resection_n"]

# chance level for cluster_fraction_pct: how much cortex a purely random
# signal needs before ANY cluster reaches the 600 mm^2 size floor, ignoring
# the "must touch the resection" requirement - a lower bound / reference,
# not the true chance level (which is strictly harder to reach). See
# chance_cluster_threshold.py in processing_spike.qmd.
resection_chance_pct = resection_metrics.metadata["derived"]["chance_pct"]

competitors = [m for m in RESECTION_METHODS if m != "wcset"]

# box + raw per-subject points (no connecting lines) + Wilcoxon
# significance stars vs. wCSET, paired by subject, FDR-corrected.
# Identical calls to the ones already cached by processing_spike.qmd's
# Statistics section.
resection_results = {}
for metric in ["peak_distance_mm", "cluster_fraction_pct"]:
    resection_results[metric] = resection_metrics.stat.wilcoxon(
        metric, group_by="Method",
        comparisons=resection_metrics.stat.build_comparisons(["wcset"], competitors),
        pairing_col="Subject", filters=FILTERS,
    )

# statistics quoted in the prose below.
_peak = resection_results["peak_distance_mm"]
_frac = resection_results["cluster_fraction_pct"]

_peak_medians = resection_metrics.metadata["derived"]["peak_median"]
_frac_medians = resection_metrics.metadata["derived"]["frac_median"]

resection_peak_median_wcset = fmt_num(_peak_medians["wcset"])
resection_peak_median_cset = fmt_num(_peak_medians["cset"])
resection_peak_median_sloreta = fmt_num(_peak_medians["sloreta"])
resection_peak_median_dspm = fmt_num(_peak_medians["dspm"])
resection_peak_median_wmne = fmt_num(_peak_medians["wmne"])
resection_peak_median_beltrami = fmt_num(_peak_medians["beltrami"])

resection_peak_p_cset = fmt_p(competitor_row(_peak, "cset")["p_corrected"])
resection_peak_r_cset = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_peak, "cset")["effect_size"])
resection_peak_p_dspm = fmt_p(competitor_row(_peak, "dspm")["p_corrected"])
resection_peak_r_dspm = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_peak, "dspm")["effect_size"])
resection_peak_p_sloreta = fmt_p(competitor_row(_peak, "sloreta")["p_corrected"])
resection_peak_r_sloreta = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_peak, "sloreta")["effect_size"])
resection_peak_p_wmne = fmt_p(competitor_row(_peak, "wmne")["p_corrected"])
resection_peak_r_wmne = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_peak, "wmne")["effect_size"])
resection_peak_p_beltrami = fmt_p(competitor_row(_peak, "beltrami")["p_corrected"])
resection_peak_r_beltrami = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_peak, "beltrami")["effect_size"])

resection_frac_median_wcset = fmt_num(_frac_medians["wcset"])
resection_frac_median_beltrami = fmt_num(_frac_medians["beltrami"])
_frac_other_medians = [_frac_medians[m] for m in competitors]
resection_frac_median_other_min = fmt_num(min(_frac_other_medians))
resection_frac_median_other_max = fmt_num(max(_frac_other_medians))

resection_frac_p_cset = fmt_p(competitor_row(_frac, "cset")["p_corrected"])
resection_frac_r_cset = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_frac, "cset")["effect_size"])
resection_frac_p_dspm = fmt_p(competitor_row(_frac, "dspm")["p_corrected"])
resection_frac_r_dspm = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_frac, "dspm")["effect_size"])
resection_frac_p_sloreta = fmt_p(competitor_row(_frac, "sloreta")["p_corrected"])
resection_frac_r_sloreta = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_frac, "sloreta")["effect_size"])
resection_frac_p_wmne = fmt_p(competitor_row(_frac, "wmne")["p_corrected"])
resection_frac_r_wmne = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_frac, "wmne")["effect_size"])
resection_frac_p_beltrami = fmt_p(competitor_row(_frac, "beltrami")["p_corrected"])
resection_frac_r_beltrami = fmt_stat(competitor_row(_frac, "beltrami")["effect_size"])

_frac_r_large = [abs(competitor_row(_frac, c)["effect_size"]) for c in ["cset", "sloreta", "dspm", "wmne"]]
resection_frac_r_large_lo = fmt_stat(min(_frac_r_large))
resection_frac_r_large_hi = fmt_stat(max(_frac_r_large))

resection_chance_pct_fmt = fmt_num(resection_chance_pct)
```

Simulation offers a controlled testbed, but real clinical data will always differ. To verify that connectivity-informed source localization remains competitive with standard clinical methods in practice — rather than trading focal precision for network sensitivity — we evaluated localization accuracy against the resected epileptogenic zone in seizure-free patients (ILAE 1, n=`{python} resection_n`).

Alongside wMNE, sLORETA, and dSPM, we also compared against a Beltrami-eigenbasis variant of wCSET — the same Laplace-Beltrami mesh eigenmodes used as a connectome surrogate in Section 3.1.4, here run as a full 6th competitor method, in the spirit of the cortical-geometry approache of @wang_geometry_2026 (Section 1).

Peak-to-resection distance behaved similarly across most methods: wCSET's median distance (`{python} resection_peak_median_wcset` mm) was descriptively the lowest, with Beltrami's the closest runner-up (`{python} resection_peak_median_beltrami` mm), ahead of sLORETA (`{python} resection_peak_median_sloreta` mm), CSET (`{python} resection_peak_median_cset` mm), and dSPM (`{python} resection_peak_median_dspm` mm), with wMNE a clear outlier (`{python} resection_peak_median_wmne` mm). Of the five paired comparisons against wCSET, only wMNE reached significance after FDR correction (Wilcoxon signed-rank, subject-paired: p_corrected `{python} resection_peak_p_wmne`, r = `{python} resection_peak_r_wmne`); CSET (p_corrected `{python} resection_peak_p_cset`, r = `{python} resection_peak_r_cset`), sLORETA (p_corrected `{python} resection_peak_p_sloreta`, r = `{python} resection_peak_r_sloreta`), dSPM (p_corrected `{python} resection_peak_p_dspm`, r = `{python} resection_peak_r_dspm`), and Beltrami (p_corrected `{python} resection_peak_p_beltrami`, r = `{python} resection_peak_r_beltrami`) were not significantly different from wCSET.

The Network Concentration Index (NCI) told a different story: wCSET required markedly less of the cortex to be marked active before a cluster first touched the resection (median `{python} resection_frac_median_wcset`% vs. `{python} resection_frac_median_other_min`–`{python} resection_frac_median_other_max`% for the other methods) — and, contrary to our initial impression of a small effect, this difference was significant for every comparison (Wilcoxon signed-rank, subject-paired, FDR-corrected: CSET p_corrected `{python} resection_frac_p_cset`, r = `{python} resection_frac_r_cset`; dSPM p_corrected `{python} resection_frac_p_dspm`, r = `{python} resection_frac_r_dspm`; sLORETA p_corrected `{python} resection_frac_p_sloreta`, r = `{python} resection_frac_r_sloreta`; wMNE p_corrected `{python} resection_frac_p_wmne`, r = `{python} resection_frac_r_wmne`; Beltrami p_corrected `{python} resection_frac_p_beltrami`, r = `{python} resection_frac_r_beltrami`), all well below the `{python} resection_chance_pct_fmt`% chance level. The effect was large for CSET, sLORETA, dSPM, and wMNE (|r| = `{python} resection_frac_r_large_lo`–`{python} resection_frac_r_large_hi`) but visibly smaller for Beltrami (r = `{python} resection_frac_r_beltrami`), whose median (`{python} resection_frac_median_beltrami`%) came closest to wCSET's on this metric too. This indicates that the top-ranked source activity is substantially more concentrated on the true epileptogenic zone for wCSET than for any comparator method — most consistently so against CSET, sLORETA, dSPM, and wMNE, and to a lesser degree against the geometry-only Beltrami variant — even though overall peak localization accuracy remains statistically comparable across methods (wMNE excepted).

Dashed line (right panel): chance level for the Network Concentration Index. Stars mark significance vs. wCSET (Wilcoxon signed-rank, subject-paired, FDR-corrected)."
